messages:
Jordan (AcmeCorp): Hey team — hitting a recurring issue where the SSE stream from /v1/streams/generate cuts out mid-response when users switch from wifi to mobile. Happens on iOS app WebView and Android Chrome. We see partial output in the app, then the client shows "stream closed" and the request never returns a final status. Started yesterday after a build bump. Anyone seen this pattern?

Alex Chen: Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the request id/correlation id for an example? Also which model + routing (hosted/dedicated) and whether retry headers were set?

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Sure — example request id: req_8f2b3c4a, model: openbb-13b (hosted), region us-west-2, routing: standard. App logs show socket close right after a network change. No explicit retry header from client.

Alex Chen: Got it. Two quick hypotheses: 1) client is aborting the HTTP request during network switch (we'd see a 499 in our ingress logs), or 2) intermediary (mobile carrier or OS) is tearing idle connections during the handover. Can you share a server-side log slice around req_8f2b3c4a?

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Server logs: 

```
[2026-02-28T09:14:21.342Z] req=8f2b3c4a start path=/v1/streams/generate conn=172.31.x.y
[2026-02-28T09:14:23.128Z] req=8f2b3c4a chunk-sent tokens=64
[2026-02-28T09:14:24.001Z] conn closed by client (code=499)
[2026-02-28T09:14:24.005Z] req=8f2b3c4a aborted, cleanup
```

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Yup see that 499 entry. The client shows a network type change event at 09:14:24.

Alex Chen: OK that matches hypothesis #1 — client closed the socket. For SSE we rely on a persistent TCP connection; if the client aborts we won't be able to finish. A couple of quick mitigations you can try client-side: 1) increase the HTTP client read timeout so it survives short handovers, 2) enable SSE auto-reconnect logic (the browser will usually do it, native WebViews sometimes don't), 3) use small heartbeat events to keep the underlying connection considered active.

Samira Patel: Jumping in from QA — we've seen iOS WKWebView tear down long-lived requests on cell/wifi handover unless the app implements background connectivity handling. For repro: 1) connect to wifi, start a 30s stream, 2) toggle airplane mode off/on or flip to mobile data, 3) watch for stream close. Repro rate ~70% on older devices.

Maria Gomez: From the runtime side — when we see a client-closed 499 we mark the request aborted; tokens already produced are not re-sent. We could improve server-side by keeping a per-request checkpoint so a resumed client could request continuation, but that's non-trivial for streaming generative APIs. Short-term: we can surface a clearer error payload and retry guidance to the SDK.

Julian Park: Can also confirm ingress logs show these metrics are spiking during the windows Jordan mentioned. We log: 

```
nginx.ingress > status=499 request_id=req_8f2b3c4a src=203.0.113.22 path=/v1/streams/generate time=2.66s
```

Julian Park: 499 = client closed before server finished sending. Not a server HTTP 5xx.

Alex Chen: Jordan — can you try a quick client-side change to confirm? In your iOS WebView, before starting the stream add a small keepalive interval (send a tiny POST to your app backend to keep socket alive) OR use the Redwood SDK streaming helper which adds a heartbeat event. If you can't change the app quickly, try reproducing with curl on mobile network to confirm network handover is the trigger:

```
# from a phone on wifi
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=openbb-13b"
```

# while curl is running flip wifi -> cellular
```

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Will try. Any server-side knobs we can turn quickly? We can't push an app update fast.

Maria Gomez: Short-term server-side options: 1) increase our HTTP keepalive TTL at the load balancer (helps if intermediate NAT is closing idle pipes), 2) ensure we emit periodic SSE comments/heartbeats from the service to keep connection activity, 3) expose a `retry_after` field in the streaming payload so clients can auto-reconnect more gracefully. I can file a small rollout for emitting ":heartbeat\n\n" every 10s for streams.

Alex Chen: Also check client timeout logic — many mobile HTTP libs treat any network change as a fatal error and call cancel() on the request. If you can trap those events and instead let the underlying socket migrate, you might avoid a 499. On Android Chrome this tends to be more tolerant than some WebViews.

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Reproduced with curl on mobile data by toggling wifi off during a 20s stream. Got same behavior and saw 499 on our side. Good to know.

Julian Park: For tracking, I'm adding a metric for streams aborted with 499 within 1-5s of client IP change. If we see a cluster tied to specific client user agents (e.g., WKWebView/Version/), we can add UA-specific guidance in the SDK.

Samira Patel: Quick repro steps to include in the ticket for triage:
- Device: iPhone X iOS 15.7.2 (WebView)
- App: AcmeCorp 4.2.1 (embedded WKWebView)
- Steps: start stream on wifi -> play output for ~10s -> toggle wifi off -> observe stream closed in 1-3s -> app shows partial result
- Logs: include server req id and client network change event timestamp

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Will provide a short video and logs to the ticket. Thank you — please advise if the short-term heartbeat rollout is possible.

Maria Gomez: I can PR a small change to the streaming proxy to emit ":heartbeat\n\n" every 10s for live streams. That will increase activity and reduce likelihood of intermediate NAT timeouts during brief handoffs. It's a low-risk change; I'll target a canary in us-west tonight.

Alex Chen: Thanks Maria. For the SDK docs, I'll add a troubleshooting note about 499 client-aborts and sample code showing graceful reconnect and resumption guidance. Example client-side pseudo-code for reconnection backoff:

```
let retryMs = 1000
function startStream(){
  openSSE(url)
  onclose = (evt) => {
    if (evt.wasClean === false) {
      setTimeout(startStream, retryMs)
      retryMs = Math.min(retryMs * 2, 10000)
    }
  }
}
```

Julian Park: One more detail — if the client reconnects quickly we could provide the last token index in a small metadata endpoint so the client can ask for a continuation from token N+1. Longer-term we should consider sequence-numbered chunks for safer resume semantics.

Jordan (AcmeCorp): All right — will test curl and share video/logs. Appreciate the quick triage.

oncall-bot: Incident queued as S-TIER: stream-abort-mobile-handovers, assigned to @Maria Gomez and @Julian Park — priority P2.

Alex Chen: I'll follow up once Maria's canary is live — Jordan please mark this thread if you see improvement so we can close. :thumbsup:

Jordan (AcmeCorp): Will do. Thanks everyone!
